correctness.rationale: For bounded q-periodic mean-zero b=|c|^2-mu, the Gram-entry tail F_m=sum_{n>=m}b_n/n^2 is O(m^-2) by bounded partial sums and Abel summation. Splitting the max(i,j) Gram matrix into two triangular sums of rank-one operators yields trace-norm bound sum_m |F_m|(sqrt(m)+sqrt(m-1))<infinity, proving trace class, not merely compactness. The exact finite diagonal-sum identity sum_{i<=N}F_i=sum_{n<=N}b_n/n+NF_{N+1} yields the conditionally convergent trace, and digamma differences give the residue formula. The author establishes the essential [0,4] spectrum of C*C via continuum Hardy kernel e^{-|u-v|/2}, its Fourier multiplier (1/4+t^2)^-1, Weyl sequences and Hilbert–Schmidt compression error; Calkin invariance gives [0,4mu] and [0,2sqrt mu]. Sang Theorems 1.1–1.2 prove C lies in the commutator ideal and characterize Rhaly Toeplitz membership; applying the one-step difference k=1 to nonconstant periodic c_n/n proves nonmembership while positivity puts |Rc| in the ideal. The small CHECKER.py performs only finite Gram/tail and example tests, explicitly not an infinite proof; an independent calculation checks q=2 indicator trace (log 2)/2.
residual_risks: The spectral step requires careful weakly-null Weyl sequences and projection to integer intervals; the proof describes rather than fully quantifies all approximation estimates.
The trace series is conditional and must not be interchanged absolutely.
q>=2, c not identically zero, possible zero entries and nonminimal period allowed.
